# model never counts unknown or missing bases as mismatches. A site whose KNOWN
# bases fit the mismatch allowance, but which overlaps N/ambiguous bases or
# runs off either end of the sequence, is reported as "not assessable" instead
# of "binds" or "mismatched".
#
# GC content is deliberately NOT used to judge data quality: a FASTA genome has
# no quality scores, and SARS-CoV-2 has genuinely AT-rich regions that a GC
# filter would wrongly throw away.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 1: DNA HELPERS (complements, degenerate bases, known bases)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A primer that binds the minus strand appears on the plus strand as its
# reverse complement, so we need a way to compute it. Ambiguity codes
# (N, Y, R, ...) are complemented too.
#
# Degenerate primers: some published primers and probes contain IUPAC codes
# (the CDC N3 probe has a Y). A primer Y matches a genome C or T.
#
# Ambiguity codes in the GENOME are read for what they say, not thrown away:
#   every base the genome letter could be is accepted by the primer -> match
#   none of them is accepted                                        -> mismatch
#   some are, some are not                                          -> unknown
# e.g. primer C vs genome Y (C or T) is unknown, primer C vs genome R (A or G)
# is a certain mismatch, primer Y vs genome Y is a certain match.
# Anything that is not a DNA letter at all (e.g. "-") is unknown.
# =============================================================================

COMPLEMENT = {
    "A": "T", "T": "A", "C": "G", "G": "C",
    "R": "Y", "Y": "R", "S": "S", "W": "W", "K": "M", "M": "K",
    "B": "V", "V": "B", "D": "H", "H": "D", "N": "N",
}

# which genome bases each primer letter accepts
IUPAC = {
    "A": "A", "C": "C", "G": "G", "T": "T",
    "R": "AG", "Y": "CT", "S": "CG", "W": "AT", "K": "GT", "M": "AC",
    "B": "CGT", "D": "AGT", "H": "ACT", "V": "ACG", "N": "ACGT",
}

KNOWN_BASES = "ACGT"   # anything else in a target counts as unknown data


def reverse_complement(seq):
    """Return the reverse complement of a DNA string (5'->3')."""
    return "".join(COMPLEMENT[base] for base in reversed(seq.upper()))


def clean_oligo(name, seq):
    """Uppercase a primer/probe and make sure every letter is a DNA/IUPAC code."""
    seq = seq.upper()
    bad = sorted(set(seq) - set(IUPAC))
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: not DNA letters: {''.join(bad)}")
    return seq


def base_matches(genome_base, primer_base):
    """True if the genome base is one the primer letter accepts."""
    return genome_base in IUPAC[primer_base]


def genome_vs_primer(genome_base, primer_base):
    """Return 'match', 'mismatch' or 'unknown' for one genome letter facing one primer letter."""
    could_be = IUPAC.get(genome_base)
    if could_be is None:
        return "unknown"   # not a DNA letter at all
    accepted = IUPAC[primer_base]
    if all(base in accepted for base in could_be):
        return "match"
    if not any(base in accepted for base in could_be):
        return "mismatch"
    return "unknown"


def expand_degenerate(seq):
    """Every plain A/C/G/T sequence a degenerate sequence stands for (YA -> CA, TA)."""
    options = [""]
    for base in seq:
        options = [option + choice for option in options for choice in IUPAC[base]]
    return options


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 2: K-MER INDEX OF THE TARGET SEQUENCE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Instead of comparing a primer to every position of the target, we record
# where every length-k word (k-mer) occurs. Looking up a primer's k-mers then
# tells us the only places worth checking. A degenerate k-mer is looked up as
# every plain k-mer it stands for.
# =============================================================================

def build_kmer_index(target, k):
    """Map each k-mer in target to the list of positions (0-based) where it starts."""
    index = {}
    for position in range(len(target) - k + 1):
        kmer = target[position:position + k]
        index.setdefault(kmer, []).append(position)
    return index


def seed_hits(index, seed):
    """All target positions where a (possibly degenerate) seed occurs exactly."""
    hits = []
    for plain in expand_degenerate(seed):
        hits += index.get(plain, [])
    return hits


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 3: COMPARING A SITE TO THE PRIMER (mismatches vs unknown bases)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Polymerase extends from the primer's 3' end, so a mismatch there matters
# far more than one at the 5' end. Each mismatch is reported as its distance
# from the 3' end: 1 = the very last (3'-terminal) base of the primer.
#
# Positions are split into two kinds:
#   mismatch - the genome letter certainly differs from what the primer accepts
#   unknown  - the genome has N/an ambiguity code that might or might not
#              match, or the position lies beyond the start or end of the
#              sequence (no data at all)
#
# Each mismatch is also described as a base change, both bases written in the
# primer's own 5'->3' direction: "primer C, genome G" means the primer has a C
# where a perfectly matching primer would need a G.
# =============================================================================

def compare_site(target, start, pattern):
    """Return (mismatch offsets, unknown offsets), left to right on the plus strand."""
    mismatches, unknowns = [], []
    for offset, primer_base in enumerate(pattern):
        position = start + offset
        if position < 0 or position >= len(target):
            unknowns.append(offset)
            continue
        verdict = genome_vs_primer(target[position], primer_base)
        if verdict == "mismatch":
            mismatches.append(offset)
        elif verdict == "unknown":
            unknowns.append(offset)
    return mismatches, unknowns


def distances_from_3prime(offsets, length, strand):
    """Convert plus-strand offsets into distances from the primer's 3' end.

    On the plus strand the primer reads left to right, so its 3' end is the
    RIGHT end of the site. On the minus strand the primer reads right to left
    along the plus strand, so its 3' end is the LEFT end of the site.
    """
    if strand == "+":
        return sorted(length - offset for offset in offsets)
    return sorted(offset + 1 for offset in offsets)


def describe_changes(target, pattern, pairs, strand):
    """Describe each mismatched (pattern offset, target position) pair as a base change."""
    changes = []
    for offset, position in pairs:
        primer_base, genome_base = pattern[offset], target[position]
        if strand == "-":   # turn both back into the primer's own direction
            primer_base, genome_base = COMPLEMENT[primer_base], COMPLEMENT[genome_base]
        changes.append({
            "from_3prime": distances_from_3prime([offset], len(pattern), strand)[0],
            "primer": primer_base,
            "genome": genome_base,
            "severity": mismatch_severity(primer_base, genome_base),
        })
    return sorted(changes, key=lambda change: change["from_3prime"])


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 3b: HOW SEVERE IS A MISMATCH? (graded, not all-or-nothing)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Not every mismatch hurts PCR equally. In a mismatch, the primer base sits
# opposite a TEMPLATE base (the complement of the genome base shown in the
# report). Measured effects near the 3' end (Stadhouders et al. 2010,
# J Mol Diagn 12:109-117; Kwok et al. 1990, Nucleic Acids Res 18:999-1005):
#   severe - primer-template A-A, G-A, A-G and C-C: these block extension
#            strongly (large rise in Ct, or no product)
#   mild   - every other pairing, e.g. G-T, T-G, T-T, T-C: the polymerase
#            often extends through them with only a small delay
# A degenerate letter counts as severe if ANY base it stands for is severe.
#
# Severity changes the 3' risk grade below; the mismatch allowance still
# counts every mismatch as 1, so the search guarantees in Section 4 hold.
# =============================================================================

SEVERE_PAIRS = {("A", "A"), ("G", "A"), ("A", "G"), ("C", "C")}   # (primer, template)


def mismatch_severity(primer_base, genome_base):
    """'severe' or 'mild' for a primer base facing the template opposite genome_base."""
    template = COMPLEMENT[genome_base]
    for primer_option in IUPAC[primer_base]:
        for template_option in IUPAC[template]:
            if (primer_option, template_option) in SEVERE_PAIRS:
                return "severe"
    return "mild"


# *****************************************************************************
# *****************************************************************************
# ***                                                                       ***
# ***   >>> USER SETTING: 3' END RISK WINDOW <<<                            ***
# ***                                                                       ***
# ***   Mismatches this many bases (or fewer) from the 3' end give the      ***
# ***   site and its product a 3' risk grade (default: 3):                  ***
# ***     high     - a severe mismatch in the window                        ***
# ***     low      - only mild mismatches in the window                     ***
# ***     possible - no mismatch, but an unknown base in the window         ***
# ***   The site still counts as binding; the grade is a warning.           ***
# ***                                                                       ***
# *****************************************************************************
# *****************************************************************************
THREE_PRIME_WINDOW = 3
RISK_ORDER = [None, "possible", "low", "high"]   # least to most worrying


def three_prime_risk(changes, unknown_from_3prime):
    """Grade the 3' end of one site: 'high', 'low', 'possible' or None."""
    near = [c for c in changes if c["from_3prime"] <= THREE_PRIME_WINDOW]
    if any(c["severity"] == "severe" for c in near):
        return "high"
    if near:
        return "low"
    if any(d <= THREE_PRIME_WINDOW for d in unknown_from_3prime):
        return "possible"
    return None


def worst_risk(*risks):
    """The most worrying of several 3' risk grades."""
    return max(risks, key=RISK_ORDER.index)

def find_binding_sites(primer_name, primer, target, index, k, max_mismatches):
    """Return every site that binds or is not assessable for this primer."""
    if len(primer) // (max_mismatches + 1) < k:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{primer_name}: {len(primer)} bases is too short to seed with k={k} "
            f"while allowing {max_mismatches} mismatches; lower k or the tolerance."
        )

    sites = []
    for strand, pattern in (("+", primer), ("-", reverse_complement(primer))):
        for start in sorted(candidate_starts(pattern, target, index, k, max_mismatches)):
            mismatches, unknowns = compare_site(target, start, pattern)
            known = len(pattern) - len(unknowns)
            if len(mismatches) > max_mismatches or known < MIN_KNOWN_BASES:
                continue  # too different (or too little data) to be a site

            # -- 4d: decide the outcome for this site
            # If the site would still fit the allowance even if EVERY unknown
            # base were a mismatch, the missing data cannot change the answer.
            if not unknowns:
                outcome, reason = "binds", ""
            elif len(mismatches) + len(unknowns) <= max_mismatches:
                outcome, reason = "binds", "binds even if every unknown base is a mismatch"
            elif start < 0:
                outcome, reason = "not assessable", "runs off the start of the sequence"
            elif start + len(pattern) > len(target):
                outcome, reason = "not assessable", "runs off the end of the sequence"
            else:
                outcome, reason = "not assessable", "overlaps N/ambiguous bases"

            changes = describe_changes(target, pattern, [(o, start + o) for o in mismatches], strand)
            unknown_from_3prime = distances_from_3prime(unknowns, len(pattern), strand)
            sites.append({
                "primer": primer_name,
                "strand": strand,
                "start": start,                    # 0-based, plus-strand coords
                "end": start + len(pattern),       # exclusive
                "outcome": outcome,
                "reason": reason,
                "mismatches": len(mismatches),
                "mismatch_from_3prime": [change["from_3prime"] for change in changes],
                "changes": changes,
                "indel": None,
                "three_prime_risk": three_prime_risk(changes, unknown_from_3prime),
                "unknown_from_3prime": unknown_from_3prime,
            })
    return sites


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 5: NEAR-MISS SEARCH FOR PRIMERS THAT FAIL (incl. insertions/deletions)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# When a primer is "mismatched", the useful scientific answer is WHY: where
# did it almost bind, and what changed there? This section finds the closest
# site, allowing at most ONE insertion or deletion (up to MAX_INDEL bases)
# plus substitutions. Differences are counted as "events":
#   each substitution = 1 event, one insertion/deletion of any length = 1 event
# so a 6-base deletion (like Alpha's spike 69-70 deletion) is ONE event,
# not 6 mismatches.
#
#   deletion  - the genome is missing bases the primer has
#   insertion - the genome has extra bases the primer does not have
#
# Only fully sequenced placements (no N, not off the ends) are considered.
# Two rules stop coincidences in a long genome from being reported:
#   - at most NEAR_MISS_MAX_EVENTS events, or NEAR_MISS_MAX_EVENTS_WITH_INDEL
#     if one of them is an insertion/deletion (a gap can sit in many places,
#     which gives coincidences many more chances)
#   - at least MIN_MATCHED_BASES primer bases must match the genome exactly
#     (a deletion leaves fewer bases to compare, which makes chance matches
#     easy: on a random 30,000-base sequence a 20-base primer found a fake
#     "6-base deletion + 1 mismatch" before this rule was added)
# So a 16-base primer can show deletions of up to 2 bases, while the 20-24
# base CDC primers can show a 6-base deletion like Alpha's 69-70 deletion.
#
# Limit: the search starts from exact k-base (5-base) stretches the primer
# shares with the genome. If the differences cut the primer into pieces all
# shorter than 5 bases, the near-miss is not found ("none close"). A 16-base
# primer is always found with up to 2 events, a 20-base primer with up to 3.
# =============================================================================

MAX_INDEL = 6
NEAR_MISS_MAX_EVENTS = 4
NEAR_MISS_MAX_EVENTS_WITH_INDEL = 2   # the indel + at most 1 substitution
MIN_MATCHED_BASES = 14


def gapped_pairs(length, left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind):
    """Pair each primer offset with the genome position it faces; also return the site end.

    kind "none":      no gap, primer offset o faces left_start + o
    kind "deletion":  primer offsets gap_at..gap_at+gap_length-1 face nothing
    kind "insertion": gap_length extra genome bases sit before primer offset gap_at
    """
    if kind == "none":
        return [(o, left_start + o) for o in range(length)], left_start + length
    left = [(o, left_start + o) for o in range(gap_at)]
    if kind == "deletion":
        right = [(o, left_start + o - gap_length) for o in range(gap_at + gap_length, length)]
        return left + right, left_start + length - gap_length
    right = [(o, left_start + o + gap_length) for o in range(gap_at, length)]
    return left + right, left_start + length + gap_length


def placements(anchor, length, max_indel=MAX_INDEL):
    """Every (left start, gap position, gap length, kind) worth trying around one seed anchor.

    A seed may sit on either side of the gap, so the left part is tried both at
    the anchor and shifted by the gap length.
    """
    yield anchor, 0, 0, "none"
    for gap_length in range(1, max_indel + 1):
        for gap_at in range(1, length):
            for left_start in {anchor, anchor - gap_length}:
                yield left_start, gap_at, gap_length, "insertion"
            if gap_at + gap_length < length:
                for left_start in {anchor, anchor + gap_length}:
                    yield left_start, gap_at, gap_length, "deletion"


def describe_indel(kind, gap_at, gap_length, length, strand):
    """Describe a gap by its kind, length and distance from the primer's 3' end."""
    if kind == "deletion":
        span = distances_from_3prime(range(gap_at, gap_at + gap_length), length, strand)
    else:
        span = distances_from_3prime([gap_at - 1, gap_at], length, strand)
    return {"kind": kind, "length": gap_length, "from_3prime": (span[0], span[-1])}


def anchors_for(pattern, index, k):
    """Start positions suggested by every exact k-mer the pattern shares with the target."""
    anchors = set()
    for offset in range(len(pattern) - k + 1):
        for hit in seed_hits(index, pattern[offset:offset + k]):
            anchors.add(hit - offset)
    return anchors


def find_near_miss(primer_name, primer, target, index, k):
    """Return the closest placement of a failed primer, or None if nothing is close."""
    best, best_key = None, None
    for strand, pattern in (("+", primer), ("-", reverse_complement(primer))):
        # -- 5a: anchors from every exact k-mer the primer shares with the target,
        # -- 5b: then score every placement around every anchor
        for anchor in anchors_for(pattern, index, k):
            for left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind in placements(anchor, len(pattern)):
                pairs, end = gapped_pairs(len(pattern), left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind)
                if left_start < 0 or end > len(target):
                    continue
                if any(base not in KNOWN_BASES for base in target[left_start:end]):
                    continue
                mismatched = [(o, p) for o, p in pairs if not base_matches(target[p], pattern[o])]
                if len(pairs) - len(mismatched) < MIN_MATCHED_BASES:
                    continue  # too few matching bases to be more than a coincidence
                events = len(mismatched) + (kind != "none")
                limit = NEAR_MISS_MAX_EVENTS if kind == "none" else NEAR_MISS_MAX_EVENTS_WITH_INDEL
                if events > limit:
                    continue  # too different to be more than a coincidence
                key = (events, gap_length)   # fewer events first, then the smaller gap
                if best_key is not None and key >= best_key:
                    continue

                # -- 5c: describe the insertion/deletion, if any
                indel = None
                if kind != "none":
                    indel = describe_indel(kind, gap_at, gap_length, len(pattern), strand)

                best_key = key
                best = {
                    "primer": primer_name,
                    "strand": strand,
                    "start": left_start,
                    "end": end,
                    "events": events,
                    "changes": describe_changes(target, pattern, mismatched, strand),
                    "indel": indel,
                }
    return best


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 5b: BINDING THROUGH A SMALL INSERTION/DELETION IN THE 5' HALF
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A 1-base insertion or deletion near a primer's 5' end usually still lets it
# bind and extend: the 3' end, where polymerase starts, is intact. So a site
# whose only gap is
#   - at most MAX_BINDING_INDEL bases long, and
#   - in the primer's 5' half (more than half the primer length from the 3' end)
# still "binds". The gap counts as 1 mismatch toward the allowance, so with
# 0 mismatches allowed no gapped site binds. A gap in the 3' half never binds;
# the near-miss search (Section 5) reports it instead.
#
# Only fully sequenced placements are used, and a gapped site is skipped where
# the same primer already has an ungapped site on that strand.
# Limit: like the near-miss search, this starts from exact 5-base stretches.
# =============================================================================

MAX_BINDING_INDEL = 1


def find_indel_sites(primer_name, primer, target, index, k, max_mismatches, existing):
    """Return extra 'binds' sites that need one small gap in the primer's 5' half."""
    if max_mismatches < 1:
        return []
    found = []
    for strand, pattern in (("+", primer), ("-", reverse_complement(primer))):
        length = len(pattern)

        # -- 5b-1: collect every allowed gapped placement
        candidates = []
        for anchor in anchors_for(pattern, index, k):
            for left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind in placements(anchor, length, MAX_BINDING_INDEL):
                if kind == "none":
                    continue
                indel = describe_indel(kind, gap_at, gap_length, length, strand)
                if indel["from_3prime"][0] <= length // 2:
                    continue  # gap is in the 3' half: not allowed to bind
                pairs, end = gapped_pairs(length, left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind)
                if left_start < 0 or end > len(target):
                    continue
                if any(base not in KNOWN_BASES for base in target[left_start:end]):
                    continue
                mismatched = [(o, p) for o, p in pairs if not base_matches(target[p], pattern[o])]
                events = len(mismatched) + 1
                if events <= max_mismatches:
                    candidates.append((events, left_start, end, indel, mismatched))

        # -- 5b-2: keep the best placement per location, skipping ungapped sites
        taken = [(s["start"], s["end"]) for s in existing
                 if s["primer"] == primer_name and s["strand"] == strand]
        for events, left_start, end, indel, mismatched in sorted(candidates, key=lambda c: (c[0], c[1])):
            if any(left_start < t_end and t_start < end for t_start, t_end in taken):
                continue
            taken.append((left_start, end))
            changes = describe_changes(target, pattern, mismatched, strand)
            found.append({
                "primer": primer_name,
                "strand": strand,
                "start": left_start,
                "end": end,
                "outcome": "binds",
                "reason": "",
                "mismatches": events,              # the gap counts as 1
                "mismatch_from_3prime": [c["from_3prime"] for c in changes],
                "changes": changes,
                "indel": indel,
                "three_prime_risk": three_prime_risk(changes, []),
                "unknown_from_3prime": [],
            })
    return found


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 6: PAIRING SITES INTO PCR PRODUCTS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A product forms when a "+" site (extending right) sits upstream of a "-"
# site (extending left) and the distance between their outer ends is within
# a plausible product length. The forward and reverse primers can pair with
# each other or with themselves, because that is what happens in a real tube.
# The probe is not a primer and never makes products.
#
# Sites that are "not assessable" are paired too, so the model can tell
# "no product possible" apart from "a product might exist, but data is
# missing". Section 7 decides which is which.
# =============================================================================

def pair_into_products(sites, min_length, max_length):
    """Return every possible product from '+' sites facing downstream '-' sites."""
    usable = [s for s in sites if s["primer"] in ("forward", "reverse")]
    plus_sites = [s for s in usable if s["strand"] == "+"]
    minus_sites = [s for s in usable if s["strand"] == "-"]
    products = []
    for left in plus_sites:
        for right in minus_sites:
            if right["end"] <= left["start"]:
                continue  # the two primers point away from each other
            length = right["end"] - left["start"]
            if min_length <= length <= max_length and right["start"] >= left["start"]:
                products.append({
                    "left": left,
                    "right": right,
                    "start": left["start"],
                    "end": right["end"],
                    "length": length,
                    "three_prime_risk": worst_risk(left["three_prime_risk"], right["three_prime_risk"]),
                })
    products.sort(key=lambda p: (p["start"], p["length"]))
    return products


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 7: OUTCOMES (per primer, per product, per assay)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per primer (forward, reverse, probe):
#   binds          - at least one site binds
#   not assessable - no site binds, but one touches missing data
#   mismatched     - no site within the mismatch allowance at all
#
# Probe inside a product: the best outcome among probe sites lying fully
# inside that product ("mismatched" if there are none).
#
# Per product (status):
#   product        - both primer sites bind (and the probe binds, if given)
#   no signal      - both primers bind but the probe does not: DNA is copied,
#                    yet a qPCR machine would see no fluorescence
#   not assessable - missing data decides it
#
# Per assay, the best product status wins, in this order:
#   product > not assessable > no signal > no product (nothing could form)
# =============================================================================

def oligo_outcome(name, sites):
    """Return 'binds', 'not assessable' or 'mismatched' for one primer or probe."""
    outcomes = {s["outcome"] for s in sites if s["primer"] == name}
    if "binds" in outcomes:
        return "binds"
    if "not assessable" in outcomes:
        return "not assessable"
    return "mismatched"


def probe_inside(product, sites):
    """Return the probe's outcome inside one product."""
    inside = [s for s in sites if s["primer"] == "probe"
              and s["start"] >= product["start"] and s["end"] <= product["end"]]
    return oligo_outcome("probe", inside)


def product_status(product, probe_given):
    """Return 'product', 'no signal' or 'not assessable' for one possible product."""
    if probe_given and product["probe"] == "mismatched":
        return "no signal"
    parts = [product["left"]["outcome"], product["right"]["outcome"]]
    if probe_given:
        parts.append(product["probe"])
    if "not assessable" in parts:
        return "not assessable"
    return "product"


def assay_outcome(products):
    """Return the assay's overall outcome from its products' statuses."""
    statuses = {p["status"] for p in products}
    for status in ("product", "not assessable", "no signal"):
        if status in statuses:
            return status
    return "no product"


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 8: THE WHOLE MODEL IN ONE CALL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Primer pair (+ optional probe) and target sequence in; one result out with
# sites, products, outcomes, near-misses and warnings.
# =============================================================================

# *****************************************************************************
# *****************************************************************************
# ***                                                                       ***
# ***   >>> USER SETTING: MISMATCH ALLOWANCE <<<                            ***
# ***                                                                       ***
# ***   max_mismatches = how many mismatches a primer may have at a site    ***
# ***                    and still count as binding (default: 2)            ***
# ***                                                                       ***
# ***   Limit: (primer length) // (max_mismatches + 1) must be >= k (5),    ***
# ***          e.g. a 16-base primer allows at most 2 mismatches.           ***
# ***                                                                       ***
# *****************************************************************************
# *****************************************************************************
def run_model(forward, reverse, target, probe=None, max_mismatches=2, k=5,
              min_length=20, max_length=1000):
    """Predict every product the primer pair could amplify from target, and explain it."""
    target = target.upper()
    index = build_kmer_index(target, k)
    oligos = {"forward": clean_oligo("forward", forward),
              "reverse": clean_oligo("reverse", reverse)}
    if probe:
        oligos["probe"] = clean_oligo("probe", probe)

    # -- 8a: binding sites for every oligo (plain sites, then small-gap sites)
    sites = []
    for name, seq in oligos.items():
        plain = find_binding_sites(name, seq, target, index, k, max_mismatches)
        sites += plain + find_indel_sites(name, seq, target, index, k, max_mismatches, plain)

    # -- 8b: products, probe check and status
    products = pair_into_products(sites, min_length, max_length)
    for product in products:
        if probe:
            product["probe"] = probe_inside(product, sites)
        product["status"] = product_status(product, probe is not None)

    # -- 8c: outcomes and near-misses for anything that failed
    outcomes = {name: oligo_outcome(name, sites) for name in oligos}
    near_misses = {name: find_near_miss(name, seq, target, index, k)
                   for name, seq in oligos.items() if outcomes[name] == "mismatched"}

    # -- 8d: warnings worth reading even when a product forms
    warnings = [f"3' risk {p['three_prime_risk']}: {p['left']['primer']} x {p['right']['primer']} "
                f"product at {p['start'] + 1}-{p['end']}"
                for p in products if p["status"] == "product" and p["three_prime_risk"]]

    return {
        "sites": sites,
        "products": products,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
        "near_misses": near_misses,
        "assay": assay_outcome(products),
        "warnings": warnings,
    }


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 9: PRINTING A READABLE REPORT (positions printed 1-based)
# =============================================================================

def format_changes(changes):
    return ", ".join(f"{c['from_3prime']} from 3': primer {c['primer']}, genome {c['genome']} "
                     f"({c['severity']})" for c in changes)


def format_indel(indel):
    low, high = indel["from_3prime"]
    size = "1 base" if indel["length"] == 1 else f"{indel['length']} bases"
    if indel["kind"] == "deletion":
        where = f"primer base {low}" if low == high else f"primer bases {low}-{high}"
        return f"deletion of {size} ({where} from 3' has no genome partner)"
    return f"insertion of {size} (extra genome bases between primer bases {low} and {high} from 3')"


def print_report(title, result):
    """Print sites, products, outcomes, near-misses and warnings."""
    print(f"\n--- {title} ---")
    print(f"sites: {len(result['sites'])}")
    for s in result["sites"]:
        line = (f"  {s['primer']:<8} strand {s['strand']}  {s['start'] + 1:>4}-{s['end']:<4} "
                f"{s['outcome']:<15} mismatches={s['mismatches']}")
        if s["changes"]:
            line += f" ({format_changes(s['changes'])})"
        if s["indel"]:
            line += f" ({format_indel(s['indel'])})"
        if s["three_prime_risk"]:
            line += f"  [3' RISK: {s['three_prime_risk'].upper()}]"
        if s["reason"]:
            line += f"  [{s['reason']}; unknown from 3' end={s['unknown_from_3prime']}]"
        print(line)

    print(f"products: {len(result['products'])}")
    for p in result["products"]:
        line = (f"  {p['left']['primer']} x {p['right']['primer']}: "
                f"{p['start'] + 1}-{p['end']}  length {p['length']} bp  status: {p['status']}")
        if "probe" in p:
            line += f"  probe: {p['probe']}"
        print(line)

    for name, miss in result["near_misses"].items():
        if miss is None:
            print(f"near-miss for {name}: none close")
            continue
        details = [format_changes(miss["changes"])] if miss["changes"] else []
        if miss["indel"]:
            details.append(format_indel(miss["indel"]))
        print(f"near-miss for {name}: strand {miss['strand']} {miss['start'] + 1}-{miss['end']}, "
              f"{miss['events']} event(s): {'; '.join(details)}")

    for warning in result["warnings"]:
        print(f"WARNING: {warning}")

    outcomes = ", ".join(f"{name} {outcome}" for name, outcome in result["outcomes"].items())
    print(f"outcome: {outcomes}, assay {result['assay']}")


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 10: READING A GENOME FILE (FASTA)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A FASTA file is one ">" header line followed by the sequence split over many
# lines. The lines are joined into one string.
# =============================================================================

def read_fasta(path):
    """Return (header, sequence) from a single-record FASTA file."""
    header, lines = "", []
    with open(path) as handle:
        for line in handle:
            line = line.strip()
            if line.startswith(">"):
                header = line[1:]
            elif line:
                lines.append(line)

407	#   each substitution = 1 event, one insertion/deletion of any length = 1 event

438	def gapped_pairs(length, left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind):
439	    """Pair each primer offset with the genome position it faces; also return the site end.

441	    kind "none":      no gap, primer offset o faces left_start + o
442	    kind "deletion":  primer offsets gap_at..gap_at+gap_length-1 face nothing
443	    kind "insertion": gap_length extra genome bases sit before primer offset gap_at
444	    """
445	    if kind == "none":
446	        return [(o, left_start + o) for o in range(length)], left_start + length
447	    left = [(o, left_start + o) for o in range(gap_at)]
448	    if kind == "deletion":

450	        return left + right, left_start + length - gap_length

455	def placements(anchor, length, max_indel=MAX_INDEL):
456	    """Every (left start, gap position, gap length, kind) worth trying around one seed anchor.

461	    yield anchor, 0, 0, "none"
462	    for gap_length in range(1, max_indel + 1):
463	        for gap_at in range(1, length):
464	            for left_start in {anchor, anchor - gap_length}:
465	                yield left_start, gap_at, gap_length, "insertion"
466	            if gap_at + gap_length < length:
467	                for left_start in {anchor, anchor + gap_length}:
468	                    yield left_start, gap_at, gap_length, "deletion"

471	def describe_indel(kind, gap_at, gap_length, length, strand):
472	    """Describe a gap by its kind, length and distance from the primer's 3' end."""

475	    else:
476	        span = distances_from_3prime([gap_at - 1, gap_at], length, strand)
477	    return {"kind": kind, "length": gap_length, "from_3prime": (span[0], span[-1])}

480	def anchors_for(pattern, index, k):
481	    """Start positions suggested by every exact k-mer the pattern shares with the target."""
482	    anchors = set()
483	    for offset in range(len(pattern) - k + 1):
484	        for hit in seed_hits(index, pattern[offset:offset + k]):
485	            anchors.add(hit - offset)
486	    return anchors
487	
488	
489	def find_near_miss(primer_name, primer, target, index, k):
490	    """Return the closest placement of a failed primer, or None if nothing is close."""
491	    best, best_key = None, None
492	    for strand, pattern in (("+", primer), ("-", reverse_complement(primer))):
493	        # -- 5a: anchors from every exact k-mer the primer shares with the target,
494	        # -- 5b: then score every placement around every anchor
495	        for anchor in anchors_for(pattern, index, k):
496	            for left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind in placements(anchor, len(pattern)):
497	                pairs, end = gapped_pairs(len(pattern), left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind)
498	                if left_start < 0 or end > len(target):
499	                    continue
500	                if any(base not in KNOWN_BASES for base in target[left_start:end]):
501	                    continue
502	                mismatched = [(o, p) for o, p in pairs if not base_matches(target[p], pattern[o])]
503	                if len(pairs) - len(mismatched) < MIN_MATCHED_BASES:
504	                    continue  # too few matching bases to be more than a coincidence
505	                events = len(mismatched) + (kind != "none")
506	                limit = NEAR_MISS_MAX_EVENTS if kind == "none" else NEAR_MISS_MAX_EVENTS_WITH_INDEL
507	                if events > limit:
508	                    continue  # too different to be more than a coincidence
509	                key = (events, gap_length)   # fewer events first, then the smaller gap
510	                if best_key is not None and key >= best_key:
511	                    continue
512	
513	                # -- 5c: describe the insertion/deletion, if any
514	                indel = None
515	                if kind != "none":
516	                    indel = describe_indel(kind, gap_at, gap_length, len(pattern), strand)
517	
518	                best_key = key
519	                best = {
520	                    "primer": primer_name,
521	                    "strand": strand,
522	                    "start": left_start,
523	                    "end": end,
524	                    "events": events,
525	                    "changes": describe_changes(target, pattern, mismatched, strand),
526	                    "indel": indel,
527	                }
528	    return best
529	
530	
531	# =============================================================================
532	# SECTION 5b: BINDING THROUGH A SMALL INSERTION/DELETION IN THE 5' HALF
533	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
534	# A 1-base insertion or deletion near a primer's 5' end usually still lets it
535	# bind and extend: the 3' end, where polymerase starts, is intact. So a site
536	# whose only gap is
537	#   - at most MAX_BINDING_INDEL bases long, and
538	#   - in the primer's 5' half (more than half the primer length from the 3' end)
539	# still "binds". The gap counts as 1 mismatch toward the allowance, so with
540	# 0 mismatches allowed no gapped site binds. A gap in the 3' half never binds;
541	# the near-miss search (Section 5) reports it instead.
542	#
543	# Only fully sequenced placements are used, and a gapped site is skipped where
544	# the same primer already has an ungapped site on that strand.
545	# Limit: like the near-miss search, this starts from exact 5-base stretches.
546	# =============================================================================
547	
548	MAX_BINDING_INDEL = 1
549	
550	
551	def find_indel_sites(primer_name, primer, target, index, k, max_mismatches, existing):
552	    """Return extra 'binds' sites that need one small gap in the primer's 5' half."""
553	    if max_mismatches < 1:
554	        return []
555	    found = []
556	    for strand, pattern in (("+", primer), ("-", reverse_complement(primer))):
557	        length = len(pattern)
558	
559	        # -- 5b-1: collect every allowed gapped placement
560	        candidates = []
561	        for anchor in anchors_for(pattern, index, k):
562	            for left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind in placements(anchor, length, MAX_BINDING_INDEL):
563	                if kind == "none":
564	                    continue
565	                indel = describe_indel(kind, gap_at, gap_length, length, strand)
566	                if indel["from_3prime"][0] <= length // 2:
567	                    continue  # gap is in the 3' half: not allowed to bind
568	                pairs, end = gapped_pairs(length, left_start, gap_at, gap_length, kind)
569	                if left_start < 0 or end > len(target):
570	                    continue
571	                if any(base not in KNOWN_BASES for base in target[left_start:end]):
572	                    continue
573	                mismatched = [(o, p) for o, p in pairs if not base_matches(target[p], pattern[o])]
574	                events = len(mismatched) + 1
575	                if events <= max_mismatches:
576	                    candidates.append((events, left_start, end, indel, mismatched))
577	
578	        # -- 5b-2: keep the best placement per location, skipping ungapped sites
579	        taken = [(s["start"], s["end"]) for s in existing
580	                 if s["primer"] == primer_name and s["strand"] == strand]
581	        for events, left_start, end, indel, mismatched in sorted(candidates, key=lambda c: (c[0], c[1])):
582	            if any(left_start < t_end and t_start < end for t_start, t_end in taken):
583	                continue
584	            taken.append((left_start, end))
585	            changes = describe_changes(target, pattern, mismatched, strand)
586	            found.append({
587	                "primer": primer_name,
588	                "strand": strand,
589	                "start": left_start,
590	                "end": end,
591	                "outcome": "binds",
592	                "reason": "",
593	                "mismatches": events,              # the gap counts as 1
594	                "mismatch_from_3prime": [c["from_3prime"] for c in changes],
595	                "changes": changes,
596	                "indel": indel,
597	                "three_prime_risk": three_prime_risk(changes, []),
598	                "unknown_from_3prime": [],
599	            })
600	    return found
601	
602	
603	# =============================================================================
604	# SECTION 6: PAIRING SITES INTO PCR PRODUCTS
605	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
606	# A product forms when a "+" site (extending right) sits upstream of a "-"
607	# site (extending left) and the distance between their outer ends is within
608	# a plausible product length. The forward and reverse primers can pair with
609	# each other or with themselves, because that is what happens in a real tube.
610	# The probe is not a primer and never makes products.
611	#
612	# Sites that are "not assessable" are paired too, so the model can tell
613	# "no product possible" apart from "a product might exist, but data is
614	# missing". Section 7 decides which is which.
615	# =============================================================================
616	
617	def pair_into_products(sites, min_length, max_length):
618	    """Return every possible product from '+' sites facing downstream '-' sites."""
619	    usable = [s for s in sites if s["primer"] in ("forward", "reverse")]
620	    plus_sites = [s for s in usable if s["strand"] == "+"]
621	    minus_sites = [s for s in usable if s["strand"] == "-"]
622	    products = []
623	    for left in plus_sites:
624	        for right in minus_sites:
625	            if right["end"] <= left["start"]:
626	                continue  # the two primers point away from each other
627	            length = right["end"] - left["start"]
628	            if min_length <= length <= max_length and right["start"] >= left["start"]:
629	                products.append({
630	                    "left": left,
631	                    "right": right,
632	                    "start": left["start"],
633	                    "end": right["end"],
634	                    "length": length,
635	                    "three_prime_risk": worst_risk(left["three_prime_risk"], right["three_prime_risk"]),
636	                })
637	    products.sort(key=lambda p: (p["start"], p["length"]))
638	    return products
639	
640	
641	# =============================================================================
642	# SECTION 7: OUTCOMES (per primer, per product, per assay)
643	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
644	# Per primer (forward, reverse, probe):
645	#   binds          - at least one site binds
646	#   not assessable - no site binds, but one touches missing data
647	#   mismatched     - no site within the mismatch allowance at all
648	#
649	# Probe inside a product: the best outcome among probe sites lying fully
650	# inside that product ("mismatched" if there are none).
651	#
652	# Per product (status):
653	#   product        - both primer sites bind (and the probe binds, if given)
654	#   no signal      - both primers bind but the probe does not: DNA is copied,
655	#                    yet a qPCR machine would see no fluorescence
656	#   not assessable - missing data decides it
657	#
658	# Per assay, the best product status wins, in this order:
659	#   product > not assessable > no signal > no product (nothing could form)
660	# =============================================================================
661	
662	def oligo_outcome(name, sites):
663	    """Return 'binds', 'not assessable' or 'mismatched' for one primer or probe."""
664	    outcomes = {s["outcome"] for s in sites if s["primer"] == name}
665	    if "binds" in outcomes:
666	        return "binds"
667	    if "not assessable" in outcomes:
668	        return "not assessable"
669	    return "mismatched"
670	
671	
672	def probe_inside(product, sites):
673	    """Return the probe's outcome inside one product."""
674	    inside = [s for s in sites if s["primer"] == "probe"
675	              and s["start"] >= product["start"] and s["end"] <= product["end"]]
676	    return oligo_outcome("probe", inside)
677	
678	
679	def product_status(product, probe_given):
680	    """Return 'product', 'no signal' or 'not assessable' for one possible product."""
681	    if probe_given and product["probe"] == "mismatched":
682	        return "no signal"
683	    parts = [product["left"]["outcome"], product["right"]["outcome"]]
684	    if probe_given:
685	        parts.append(product["probe"])
686	    if "not assessable" in parts:
687	        return "not assessable"
688	    return "product"
689	
690	
691	def assay_outcome(products):
692	    """Return the assay's overall outcome from its products' statuses."""
693	    statuses = {p["status"] for p in products}
694	    for status in ("product", "not assessable", "no signal"):
695	        if status in statuses:
696	            return status
697	    return "no product"
698	
699	
700	# =============================================================================
701	# SECTION 8: THE WHOLE MODEL IN ONE CALL
702	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
703	# Primer pair (+ optional probe) and target sequence in; one result out with
704	# sites, products, outcomes, near-misses and warnings.
705	# =============================================================================
706	
707	# *****************************************************************************
708	# *****************************************************************************
709	# ***                                                                       ***
710	# ***   >>> USER SETTING: MISMATCH ALLOWANCE <<<                            ***
711	# ***                                                                       ***
712	# ***   max_mismatches = how many mismatches a primer may have at a site    ***
713	# ***                    and still count as binding (default: 2)            ***
714	# ***                                                                       ***
715	# ***   Limit: (primer length) // (max_mismatches + 1) must be >= k (5),    ***
716	# ***          e.g. a 16-base primer allows at most 2 mismatches.           ***
717	# ***                                                                       ***
718	# *****************************************************************************
719	# *****************************************************************************
720	def run_model(forward, reverse, target, probe=None, max_mismatches=2, k=5,
721	              min_length=20, max_length=1000):
722	    """Predict every product the primer pair could amplify from target, and explain it."""
723	    target = target.upper()
724	    index = build_kmer_index(target, k)
725	    oligos = {"forward": clean_oligo("forward", forward),
726	              "reverse": clean_oligo("reverse", reverse)}
727	    if probe:
728	        oligos["probe"] = clean_oligo("probe", probe)
729	
730	    # -- 8a: binding sites for every oligo (plain sites, then small-gap sites)
731	    sites = []
732	    for name, seq in oligos.items():
733	        plain = find_binding_sites(name, seq, target, index, k, max_mismatches)
734	        sites += plain + find_indel_sites(name, seq, target, index, k, max_mismatches, plain)
735	
736	    # -- 8b: products, probe check and status
737	    products = pair_into_products(sites, min_length, max_length)
738	    for product in products:
739	        if probe:
740	            product["probe"] = probe_inside(product, sites)
741	        product["status"] = product_status(product, probe is not None)
742	
743	    # -- 8c: outcomes and near-misses for anything that failed
744	    outcomes = {name: oligo_outcome(name, sites) for name in oligos}
745	    near_misses = {name: find_near_miss(name, seq, target, index, k)
746	                   for name, seq in oligos.items() if outcomes[name] == "mismatched"}
747	
748	    # -- 8d: warnings worth reading even when a product forms
749	    warnings = [f"3' risk {p['three_prime_risk']}: {p['left']['primer']} x {p['right']['primer']} "
750	                f"product at {p['start'] + 1}-{p['end']}"
751	                for p in products if p["status"] == "product" and p["three_prime_risk"]]
752	
753	    return {
754	        "sites": sites,
755	        "products": products,
756	        "outcomes": outcomes,
757	        "near_misses": near_misses,
758	        "assay": assay_outcome(products),
759	        "warnings": warnings,
760	    }
761	
762	
763	# =============================================================================
764	# SECTION 9: PRINTING A READABLE REPORT (positions printed 1-based)
765	# =============================================================================
766	
767	def format_changes(changes):
768	    return ", ".join(f"{c['from_3prime']} from 3': primer {c['primer']}, genome {c['genome']} "
769	                     f"({c['severity']})" for c in changes)
770	
771	
772	def format_indel(indel):
773	    low, high = indel["from_3prime"]
774	    size = "1 base" if indel["length"] == 1 else f"{indel['length']} bases"
775	    if indel["kind"] == "deletion":
776	        where = f"primer base {low}" if low == high else f"primer bases {low}-{high}"
777	        return f"deletion of {size} ({where} from 3' has no genome partner)"
778	    return f"insertion of {size} (extra genome bases between primer bases {low} and {high} from 3')"
779	
780	
781	def print_report(title, result):
782	    """Print sites, products, outcomes, near-misses and warnings."""
783	    print(f"\n--- {title} ---")
784	    print(f"sites: {len(result['sites'])}")
785	    for s in result["sites"]:
786	        line = (f"  {s['primer']:<8} strand {s['strand']}  {s['start'] + 1:>4}-{s['end']:<4} "
787	                f"{s['outcome']:<15} mismatches={s['mismatches']}")
788	        if s["changes"]:
789	            line += f" ({format_changes(s['changes'])})"
790	        if s["indel"]:
791	            line += f" ({format_indel(s['indel'])})"
792	        if s["three_prime_risk"]:
793	            line += f"  [3' RISK: {s['three_prime_risk'].upper()}]"
794	        if s["reason"]:
795	            line += f"  [{s['reason']}; unknown from 3' end={s['unknown_from_3prime']}]"
796	        print(line)
797	
798	    print(f"products: {len(result['products'])}")
799	    for p in result["products"]:
800	        line = (f"  {p['left']['primer']} x {p['right']['primer']}: "
801	                f"{p['start'] + 1}-{p['end']}  length {p['length']} bp  status: {p['status']}")
802	        if "probe" in p:
803	            line += f"  probe: {p['probe']}"
804	        print(line)
805	
806	    for name, miss in result["near_misses"].items():
807	        if miss is None:
808	            print(f"near-miss for {name}: none close")
809	            continue
810	        details = [format_changes(miss["changes"])] if miss["changes"] else []
811	        if miss["indel"]:
812	            details.append(format_indel(miss["indel"]))
813	        print(f"near-miss for {name}: strand {miss['strand']} {miss['start'] + 1}-{miss['end']}, "
814	              f"{miss['events']} event(s): {'; '.join(details)}")
815	
816	    for warning in result["warnings"]:
817	        print(f"WARNING: {warning}")
818	
819	    outcomes = ", ".join(f"{name} {outcome}" for name, outcome in result["outcomes"].items())
820	    print(f"outcome: {outcomes}, assay {result['assay']}")
821	
822	
823	# =============================================================================
824	# SECTION 10: READING A GENOME FILE (FASTA)
825	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
826	# A FASTA file is one ">" header line followed by the sequence split over many
827	# lines. The lines are joined into one string.
828	# =============================================================================
829	
830	def read_fasta(path):
831	    """Return (header, sequence) from a single-record FASTA file."""
832	    header, lines = "", []
833	    with open(path) as handle:
834	        for line in handle:
835	            line = line.strip()
836	            if line.startswith(">"):
837	                header = line[1:]
838	            elif line:
839	                lines.append(line)

TEST CASES: FIRST MODEL: FACTOR: SPECIFICITY (version 4)
=========================================================
Model: journal/first_model_factor_specificity.py
Tests: journal/test_first_model_factor_specificity.py
Run:   python3 journal/test_first_model_factor_specificity.py
Real-data check: python3 journal/cdc_reference_check.py  (see the end of this file)

All cases use fake 16-base primers and a fake target built by hand,
so every expected answer is worked out on paper before running.

Fake pieces:
  Forward primer   GTTCAGAGCTACTGAC
  Reverse primer   TCCGATAGTCAGCTTG
  Reverse site     CAAGCTGACTATCGGA   (reverse primer as it appears on the + strand)
  Insert / probe   CGTACGTTGCATGCCTAGGT
  Filler           AAAA...            (poly-A, no primer can bind it)
  Amplicon         forward + insert + reverse site = 16 + 20 + 16 = 52 bp

Outcomes:
  Primer/probe: binds / mismatched / not assessable
  Assay:        product / not assessable / no signal / no product
  Positions are 1-based (first base of the target = 1).
  ^ marks a planted mismatch, N or extra base in the target.
  Base changes read "primer C, genome G": the primer has C where a
  perfect primer would need G (both in the primer's own direction).
  Severity: severe (primer-template A-A, G-A, A-G, C-C) or mild (all others).
  3' risk: high (severe mismatch within 3 bases of the 3' end), low (mild
  only), possible (unknown base there), or none.


CORE CASES (version 1)
----------------------

Case 1 - Exact match
  Mismatches allowed: 0
  Target:   AAAAAAAAAAGTTCAGAGCTACTGACCGTACGTTGCATGCCTAGGTCAAGCTGACTATCGGAAAAAAAAAAA
  Outcome:  forward binds, reverse binds -> product, 52 bp (positions 11-62)
  Meaning:  Baseline: perfect primers give exactly one product of the right
            size. If this fails, nothing else can be trusted.

Case 2 - Reverse strand
  Mismatches allowed: 0
  Target:   TTTTTTTTTTTCCGATAGTCAGCTTGACCTAGGCATGCAACGTACGGTCAGTAGCTCTGAACTTTTTTTTTT
            (Case 1 target, reverse-complemented)
  Outcome:  forward binds, reverse binds -> product, 52 bp
            (the reverse primer is now the "+" site, forward the "-" site)
  Meaning:  Primers can bind either DNA strand; a model checking only one
            strand would miss real products.

Case 3a - Mismatches at the 3' end, none allowed
  Mismatches allowed: 0
  Target:   AAAAAAAAAAGTTCAGAGCTACTGAGCGTACGTTGCATGCCTAGGTTAAGCTGACTATCGGAAAAAAAAAAA
                                     ^                    ^
  Outcome:  forward mismatched, reverse mismatched -> no product
            near-misses: forward 1 from 3': primer C, genome G (severe)
                         reverse 1 from 3': primer G, genome A (mild)
  Meaning:  With zero tolerance, one mismatch per primer loses the product,
            and the near-miss says exactly which base change caused it.

Case 3b - Same target, 1 mismatch allowed
  Mismatches allowed: 1
  Target:   (same as 3a)
  Outcome:  forward binds, reverse binds -> product, 52 bp
            forward site 3' risk HIGH (C opposite template C: severe)
            reverse site 3' risk LOW  (G opposite template T: mild)
            product takes the worse grade: HIGH; WARNING printed
  Meaning:  The user-set allowance works, and 3'-end mismatches are graded
            by how much that kind of mismatch actually hurts PCR.

Case 3c - Mismatch at the 5' end
  Mismatches allowed: 1
  Target:   AAAAAAAAAACTTCAGAGCTACTGACCGTACGTTGCATGCCTAGGTCAAGCTGACTATCGGAAAAAAAAAAA
                      ^
  Outcome:  forward binds (16 from 3': primer G, genome C, mild), reverse
            binds -> product, 52 bp, no 3' risk
  Meaning:  Position counting runs the right direction, and a harmless 5'
            mismatch does not raise a warning.

Case 4 - Multiple products
  Mismatches allowed: 0
....
Case 22 - 1-base deletion in the primer's 5' half
  Mismatches allowed: 1, then 0
  Target:   AAAAAAAAAAGTCAGAGCTACTGACCGTACGTTGCATGCCTAGGTCAAGCTGACTATCGGAAAAAAAAAAA
            (one T removed from the start of the forward site)
  Outcome:  tolerance 1: forward binds through a 1-base deletion (15 from 3'),
                         product 51 bp (one base shorter)
            tolerance 0: forward mismatched (the gap counts as 1 mismatch)
  Meaning:  A small gap far from the 3' end usually still lets the primer
            extend. Version 3 always called it a failure.

Case 22b - 1-base deletion in the primer's 3' half
  Mismatches allowed: 1
  Target:   AAAAAAAAAAGTTCAGAGCTACTACCGTACGTTGCATGCCTAGGTCAAGCTGACTATCGGAAAAAAAAAAA
            (the G 3 bases from the forward primer's 3' end removed)
  Outcome:  forward mismatched; near-miss: deletion of 1 base, 3 from 3'
  Meaning:  A gap near the 3' end is not allowed to bind; the near-miss
            explains why the primer fails.


SEARCH CHECKS (version 4)
-------------------------

Case 23 - Fast search vs slow every-position search
  Setup:    200 random 300-base targets with mutated primer copies, scattered
            N/Y bases and cut ends; mismatch allowances 0, 1 and 2
  Outcome:  all 600 searches find exactly the same sites (1361 sites)
  Meaning:  The k-mer shortcut never skips a real site.

Case 24 - No invented near-misses
  Setup:    CDC N1 primers and probe on a random 30,000-base sequence
  Outcome:  no binding sites, no near-misses
  Meaning:  Guards against the chance "6-base deletion" match found while
            building version 3.


REAL DATA: CDC PANEL ON THE REFERENCE GENOME (cdc_reference_check.py)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
  Genome:   NC_045512.2 (Wuhan-Hu-1, 29,903 bases), mismatch allowance 2

  Assay  Product (1-based)  Length  Published  Probe  Result
  N1     28287-28358        72 bp   73 bp      binds  FAIL on size only (see note)
  N2     29164-29230        67 bp   67 bp      binds  PASS
  N3     28681-28752        72 bp   72 bp      binds  PASS (probe has a Y)
  RP     none               -       -          -      PASS (human gene: no product)

  Every primer matches the reference perfectly, each assay gives exactly
  one product at the verified primer positions, and every probe binds.

  Note on N1: the table lists 73 bp, but the table's own published
  coordinates (28303-28374) and verified coordinates (28287-28358) both span
  72 bases. The model is reporting the span correctly; the 73 bp value in the
  primer table needs checking against Lu et al. (2020).
